reading.title: How Families Prepare for Bad Weather
reading.purpose: Learn practical steps that help people stay calm and safe during storms or floods.
paras: Big storms, floods, and fires can hit with little notice. A simple plan ahead of time helps a home know what to do when an emergency, a sudden and grave event needing fast steps, arrives.

First, learn the signs of risk near you. A down wire or deep fast water is a real hazard that could cause harm. When a storm radio sounds its loud alarm, listen close to local leaders instead of guessing.

If leaders tell your block to evacuate, leave the unsafe spot right away and head to a safe hall. Do not drive through deep water. A car can get stranded, stuck in high water with no way to move. If folks get stuck, trained teams come by boat to rescue them and bring them to dry land.

Strong fear is normal in a tough spot. Your hands may tremble and shake from cold or stress, yet do not let panic take hold so you can think clearly. Take a slow breath, brace yourself for hard steps, and go down your list one by one.
Clean water, hand lamps, and warm wraps help homes survive bad storms safely until help comes.

choices: listening closely to a loud weather radio signal
stuck in a place and unable to get away
packing clean water and flashlights before a storm
leaving a neighborhood early to reach a shelter
qs.why: Paragraph 3 explains that a car in high water can get stranded, "stuck in high water with no way to move."

qs.q: Which sentence gives two examples of a hazard?
choices: First, learn the signs of risk near you.
A down wire or deep fast water is a real hazard that could cause harm.
When a storm radio sounds its loud alarm, listen close to local leaders instead of guessing.
Strong fear is normal in a tough spot.
qs.why: This sentence names a down wire and deep fast water as real hazards.

ev.text: A down wire or deep fast water is a real hazard that could cause harm.

qs.q: Why does the reading advise people not to let panic take hold?
choices: Staying calm helps them think clearly and follow their plan.
Storm radios stop working whenever people feel cold or stressed.
Rescue boats only pick up homes that already own three lamps.
Evacuating early is only needed during fires and never during floods.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 explains that avoiding panic lets you think clearly and go down your list one by one.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Driving through deep water is the quickest way to reach a neighborhood hall.
Plans, calm thinking, and warnings keep people safe in storms.
Every storm requires rescue teams to travel by boat through flooded city streets.
Hand lamps and warm wraps are the only things needed during a big fire.
qs.why: The reading explains how plans, hazard awareness, evacuation, calmness, and supplies help people survive emergencies.
